A: Clinical photographs showing characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism (dolichocephaly, hypoplastic alae nasi, micrognathia), marfanoid habitus, mild thoracic scoliosis, and pes planus in a child with Loeys-Dietz syndrome. C: Clinical photographs showing translucent skin with visible superficial veins and flat feet in an adult patient with Loeys-Dietz syndrome.

D: Clinical photograph showing bilateral clubfoot (talipes equinovarus), a musculoskeletal manifestation reported in this Loeys-Dietz syndrome case. E: Clinical photograph of the back showing kyphoscoliosis, a spinal deformity associated with Loeys-Dietz syndrome as described in the caption. F: Clinical photograph of the lateral torso showing kyphoscoliosis, demonstrating the spinal curvature associated with Loeys-Dietz syndrome.

We describe a maternally inherited TGFBR1 mutation in mosaicism. The mother showed recurrent buccal artery hemorrhage that was managed surgically. She also experienced severe reduction in visual acuity secondary to unexplained vitreous detachment. Cardiovascular MRA showed generalized cerebrovascular asymmetry, mild dilatation of the proximal abdominal aorta, and multiple deep myocardial crypts in the inferior basal segment of the left ventricle, with a dysplastic aspect of the mitral papillary muscle architecture (Fig. 2).
